title: POC latency deep-tune standup
summary: Weekly POC sync to review TTFT and streaming latency runs, evaluate sequence-length policy changes and kernel selection impact. SE presented new int8 mixed-quant runs and an alternative kernel plan for long tail seqs. Customers raised question about VPC egress and audit latency for bench runs. Agreed next steps: rerun 1) 2k token mixed-int8 stream with kv-cache warmup, 2) golden prompt set with disabled dynamic batching, and 3) timeline for Dedicated baseline comparison.
topics: TTFT measurements and drift vs baseline
Sequence length distribution impact and synthetic long-tail tests
Kernel selection: fused attention vs chunked matmul
Operational concerns: VPC egress, audit logs, benchmark reproducibility
next_steps: Redwood to share run artifacts and raw CSV for 2026-03-04 mixed-int8 stream (s3 link)
EdgeStream to provide golden prompt set and top-1% longest queries by Thursday 2026-03-07
SE to schedule kernel-level repro on Dedicated staging by 2026-03-10
AE to send updated commercial note with pilot pricing note and committed baseline comparisons
action_items: Jonah: upload raw bench CSV + consolidated latency plot to s3://redwood-pocs/edge-stream/0305 (due 2026-03-06)
Carlos: export top 200 long-tail queries and share sample prompts (due 2026-03-07)
Maya: circulate trimmed security summary and confirm SSO contact (due 2026-03-08)
Priya: confirm availability for Dedicated staging window 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-11 (due 2026-03-06)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: alright we're live, thanks everyone for joining the 03-05 POC standup. we've got 40 minutes on the calendar. Jonah, want to kick with the run highlights?
[00:14] Jonah Patel: yeah sure, uh quick context — we ran the mixed-int8 streaming test last night, same model family as before, note we unintentionally used the 1.25x longer context which bumped the median sequence length, so some numbers skewed a bit. raw CSV is in s3 link, I'll upload the cleaned plot in a minute.
[00:29] Carlos Vega: quick question — when you say mixed-int8 do you mean per-channel per-tensor quant or the new mixed scheme you mentioned earlier? i.e. is KV still in FP16?
[00:41] Jonah Patel: good call — KV remained FP16 for the run, weights were mixed int8 on matmuls, and we used fallback to int4 on a couple small kernels, that fallback path may have caused some small jitter.
[00:58] Priya Menon: jitter as in TTFT jitter? we need very consistent time-to-first-token for our demo.
[01:04] Jonah Patel: yep TTFT saw a median of 210ms on the short prompts, baseline was 180ms — but p95 climbed to 520ms for queries hitting long-tail seqs. we traced p95 to a kernel switch path where fused attention wasn't used because sequence length crossed the threshold.
[01:24] Maya Chen: to be clear, baseline numbers were from your earlier Dedicated-staging run right?
[01:29] Jonah Patel: correct, the baseline was Dedicated-staging last week — and that run used fused attention everywhere since the sequence lengths stayed <512. last night's streaming with 1.25x context pushed a slice into the chunked matmul path.
[01:48] Anika Roy: can you explain chunked matmul vs fused attention quickly? mine's a bit fuzzy — our infra folks want to know the cost/latency tradeoff.
[01:56] Jonah Patel: sure — fused attention is our low-latency kernel for typical seq lengths, gives good memory packing and single-kernel pass. chunked matmul chops sequences and runs multiple matmuls, so overhead and extra kernel launches add to latency, especially on small batches. it's better memory-wise for huge contexts but costs TTFT.
[02:19] Carlos Vega: is there a knob to keep fused attention beyond the threshold? maybe at the expense of memory?
[02:24] Jonah Patel: you can force kernel selection in config — we usually auto-select based on sequence distribution to avoid OOM. but for pilot you can pin fused-attn with a memory guard; we tried a pin in one run and saw p95 drop but memory usage spiked.
[02:37] Priya Menon: this is the core tradeoff we care about. demo slo is p95 < 300ms.
[02:43] Maya Chen: okay noted. Jonah, can you run a pinned fused-attn test with KV pre-warm and capped batch size? try also toggling dynamic batching off.
[02:51] Jonah Patel: yep will do.
[02:54] [00:03:00] Maya Chen: other notable things from the benchmark?
[03:05] Jonah Patel: streaming chunk size matters — we used 64-token chunks which introduced backpressure on the client and small extra shards per response; when we reduced to 32-token chunking TTFT improved slightly but throughput dropped. there's a tradeoff between chunk size and network overhead, also client lib is sensitive — we saw partial reassembly delays.
[03:29] Carlos Vega: our frontend uses the client lib for reassembly — we can adjust chunk size client side but we'd prefer server-side sensible defaults.
[03:36] Maya Chen: we can default to 48 tokens for your workload and tune.
[03:40] Anika Roy: also curious — did the run enable prefix caching? some of our queries repeat long warmup prefixes.
[03:47] Jonah Patel: yes prefix/KV cache warmup was enabled but the warmup window in the run was small. if we do a dedicated warmup (pre-roll a 128 prompt for the session) the TTFT for subsequent requests drops significantly.
[04:02] Priya Menon: that might be enough for our demo flows. can you quantify warmup benefit? like median delta?
[04:10] Jonah Patel: ballpark — after a 128-token warmup, median on short prompts went from 210ms to 150ms in our test. p95 improved as well but long-tail still suffers if kernel switches happen.
[04:25] [00:06:00] Carlos Vega: about quantization: are we comfortable with mixed-int8 in production? audit/regulatory folks will ask about determinism and logits shift.
[04:36] Maya Chen: totally—we have eval diffs from the model team; the mixed-int8 path had less than 0.6% top-1 decode diffs on the golden set. we can share the eval diff report.
[04:47] Anika Roy: can we run a regression alert for the pilot so if quality shifts beyond 1% you notify?
[04:53] Jonah Patel: yes Redwood Optimize can hook into your evals and raise a regression alert; we'll set up an eval monitor for the golden prompts.
[05:01] Priya Menon: on security — we need assurance about VPC egress during bench uploads and also audit logs for bench runs. last week we saw unclear egress in the staging logs.
[05:11] Maya Chen: action: i'll send a boiled-down security brief and the SSO contact. bench uploads can be restricted to the VPC peering path, we'll confirm the exact route.
[05:20] Carlos Vega: sweet. also who owns the benchmarking script? we had to re-run locally because the csv format was slightly different.
[05:26] Jonah Patel: guilty — i modified the runner to log additional kernel metadata; i'll publish both raw and normalized CSVs and include a header README.
[05:34] [00:08:00] Anika Roy: quick question on Dedicated vs Hosted baseline — for cost modeling we need a Dedicated baseline run with the same quant config, can you schedule that?
[05:44] Maya Chen: yes we'll run Dedicated-staging baseline with mixed-int8 pinned kernels and KV warmup. Jonah, schedule window?
[05:50] Jonah Patel: i can schedule during your suggested window 03-09 to 03-11; need priya to confirm maintenance window.
[05:58] Priya Menon: tentatively 03-10 morning looks ok.
[06:03] Maya Chen: ok lock 03-10 09:00 UTC for Dedicated staging run, we'll confirm in the notes.
[06:10] [00:10:00] Carlos Vega: one more nit — TTFT measurement method: your CSV shows server-time-first-byte, but our instrumentation measures client-accept-time which adds 10-20ms. can we align metrics?
[06:21] Jonah Patel: yes we'll add client-side hooks and produce both metrics; i'll add a normalized column in the next CSV.
[06:29] Maya Chen: great. moving on — kernel selection heuristics: Jonah, you proposed a smoothing window to avoid frequent kernel flips for queries that hover around threshold?
[06:38] Jonah Patel: right, a short-term hysteresis where if sequence length changes but previous N requests used fused-attn we'd keep fused for M seconds unless memory pressure exceeds X. that reduced flip rate by ~70% in initial sim.
[06:52] Anika Roy: that seems promising. does that increase chance of OOM for extreme bursts?
[06:57] Jonah Patel: it's a balance — the hysteresis parameter combined with a memory guard prevents OOM. we'd surface a memory alert earlier.
[07:05] [00:12:00] Priya Menon: about streaming backpressure — our clients sometimes drop connection mid-stream and that spikes server resource. any mitigation?
[07:13] Jonah Patel: yes we added soft connection timeouts and chunked-buffer GC; also client lib improvements to ACK chunks earlier helped. we'll share a patched client lib build.
[07:23] Carlos Vega: can you share the patched client build? we can test it in staging.
[07:27] Jonah Patel: will attach link to the repo in the notes.
[07:31] [00:14:00] Maya Chen: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[07:36] Carlos Vega: quick point — competitor ManagedCloudAI reached out to compare pricing, they promise lower token price but no dedicated tuning or kernel controls.
[07:44] Maya Chen: noted. we'll include that in the pricing note.
[07:49] Jonah Patel: for reproducing p95, i'll also add a run with forced chunked path to show worst-case.
[07:56] Priya Menon: good. and please include the golden prompt set in the eval monitor.
[07:59] Jonah Patel: yes.
[08:02] [00:16:00] Anika Roy: two asks from me: 1) share eval-diff report, 2) timeline for Dedicated baseline.
[08:10] Maya Chen: we'll share eval-diff and lock the Dedicated window for 03-10 09:00 UTC.
[08:15] Carlos Vega: timeline wise, if Dedicated run is green we can flip pilot to Dedicated for the demo next week.
[08:21] Maya Chen: great. any final blockers?
[08:24] Priya Menon: nothing else.
[08:26] Maya Chen: cool, thanks everyone. Jonah will upload artifacts, i'll send security note and pricing, Carlos and Priya to share golden prompts and maintenance window confirmation. we'll reconvene next Tuesday same time.
[08:40] [00:41:00] (meeting ended)
